decisions.rationale: Known-speaker diarization attributes the entire selected causal-ground and circularity argument to Pine. Schmid's brief acknowledgment ends just before the selected passage begins; it supplies no premise and receives no credit or penalty. The surrounding audio preserves Pine's qualification about different kinds of reciprocal causality.

Known-speaker diarization confirms Pine's survey of divine ideas and his rational-versus-real distinction. Near the caption span's end, Fradd gives only acknowledgments, and approximately the first third of a second of Schmid's next response overlaps the caption boundary. Those words are surrounding context, not part of Pine's scored argument; all substantive selected reasoning and the quote candidate are Pine's.
